en: *Preface to the *Mishisuo jing* (The Scripture on the Path of Delusion in Listening), One Scroll.* At that time, Mīśika spoke the Preface to the *Sādharmya-sūtra*, saying: "Who can explain the variations in the many and few views?
Who can explain the difficult-to-quell matters within the meaning of the sūtras? Where is the Tathāgata revealed after his passing?"
Where does he abide? Among all Buddhas,
non-humans, the devas who deliberate, and arhats—
whoever beholds the World-Honored One among sentient beings.
No one can see the World-Honored One.
What person possesses such majesty as to be able to see the World-Honored One?
For this reason, the countenance of the World-Honored One resembles the wind.
Who can perceive the wind?
The World-Honored One, before even a short time had passed, traveled through the various abodes of the world;
because this person dwelt there, they were imbued with the aura of the World-Honored One.
Only then did he manage to survive;
only then did he find peace at home,
until his mind reached its destination.
From sunrise until sunset,
wherever the mind goes as it dwells upon perceptions, he reaches them all;
his body abides in clarity, bliss, and tranquility, dwelling securely in meditative concentration.
In the heavens there are all Buddhas;
for this reason, they circulate through the world by means of the wind.
Wherever the wind flows, there is nowhere it does not reach.
The Celestial Honored One always dwells in the place of tranquil liberation and bliss;
yet the fruition of his rewards reaches everywhere throughout the world for all beings.
Who knows that it is the wind moving?
One hears only the sound, yet does not see its form at all.
No one recognizes that his countenance is upright and handsome;
how could it be anything other than neither yellow, nor white, nor azure?
Likewise, no one knows where the wind dwells when it is at its strongest.
The Celestial Honored One possesses divine majesty of his own;
though he dwells in one place,
no one can apprehend him where he resides.
There is neither birth nor death,
nor is there any place where beings encounter one another;
having fashioned heaven and earth, he sought [them].
Never having existed within the world,
lacking divine power, he constantly receives the karmic conditions for the longevity and bliss of an immortal.
In times of urgency, people often invoke the name of the Buddha;
yet there are many who lack understanding.
Terms such as "invoking the spirits" (喚神) and "comparing to the Celestial Honored Ones" (比天尊) are also transcribed as "Zhi-zun" (旨尊) and "Zhi-le" (旨樂);
these are all local vernacular expressions used by the common people.
I have been apart from the World-Honored One for many long periods;
every time I have had faith, I have dwelt [in his presence].
The World-Honored One’s understanding of people’s intentions is not slight.
Who can repay the Buddha’s compassionate grace?
One should deliberate upon this and clearly understand it.
One does not practice evil.
The heavens provide sustenance through their supernatural power;
when one attains a human body, it reaches its full measure.
It is likewise fitting for sentient beings to reflect that wherever there is a human body, life, or the vessel of the breaths,
it is entirely the Celestial Honored One who causes these things to be so.
All sentient beings undergo transmigration;
their bodies abide within the realm of earth and water,
which is thus transformed and fashioned from subtle atoms.
All sentient beings gave rise to wholesome thoughts.
Reflecting within themselves,
they realized that all who are born must die.
All sentient beings are utterly abandoned;
the bodies and lives of sentient beings are rendered lifeless by the wind.
At the time of death,
the winds depart from the sentient being;
the mind and consciousness are then without wind.
They subsist on wind. When wind departs from sentient beings,
there comes a time of its departure and its remaining.
For what reason do people not see the color of the wind as it moves—
whether it be yellow, crimson, green, or any other color?
Based on this, the wind is not seen.
If sentient beings are themselves the Way,
then where does the Honored One of Heaven reside?
Sentient beings transcend the Way.
For what reason do sentient beings, while remaining within their transgressions, not see the World-Honored One? For what reason do they see the World-Honored One for themselves?
The World-Honored One is not the same as a human being.
Furthermore, who is able to see sentient beings?
No one dares to approach the Honored One.
Sentient beings possess virtuous merit and virtuous conditions.
Only then was it possible to see the World-Honored One;
originally, no one in the world had seen him.
How, then, could he have been recognized?
Sentient beings do not see the heavens for themselves; yet,
by cultivating merit for themselves,
they do not fall into the evil realms or the hells.
They immediately attain what is attained by the gods;
for example, there are multitudes with evil karma who fall into the evil realms.
They do not perceive the fruit of clarity,
nor do they attain the heavenly realms.
May all sentient beings reflect well upon this for themselves.
The Emperor and the Sovereign are great.
Those who serve and nourish the various wicked sentient beings under them may,
through diligent devotion to the state, receive many rewards, honors, and official positions.
And he bestowed immeasurable, immeasurable varieties of vegetables.
If there are sentient beings who do not serve the great heavens or commit various evils, [they shall receive these].
Furthermore, he did not receive instructions on conduct,
nor did he obtain an official post,
nor was there any reward granted to him.
They were immediately sentenced to banishment or transport; they were immediately sentenced to death.
This was not because great evils had spontaneously arrived from heaven.
Because the seeds of karma from previous lives have ripened into a complete mass of fruit,
there are sentient beings who have transgressed;
first, one must contemplate the retribution of one's own body.
The Celestial Honored One granted his permission; through arduous effort, he first established the principle for the multitude of sentient beings.
The Buddha does not stand far off;
it is up to each person to take responsibility for themselves.
Goodness brings good fortune;
evil brings evil conditions.
Thus it is with ignorant sentient beings.
He then carved wooden figures of camels, elephants, oxen, donkeys, horses, and other creatures, as well as deer; yet,
though he fashioned their forms,
he could not bestow life upon them.
Sentient beings possess cognition;
they personally measure their own conditions and fruits,
and all that they perceive.
Furthermore, one knows for oneself that both are indeed real;
therefore, they exist in this present life.
There are many sentient beings who,
having themselves become various groups and various leaders,
consider these matters to be the work of the Celestial Honored One.
Consequently, they were unable to preserve their lives;
sentient beings, having deluded themselves,
fashioned an elephant out of gold.
He fashioned silver statues and bronze statues, as well as images of yakṣas and wooden statues;
furthermore, he produced various kinds of livestock and created human-like figures.
They fashioned horses that resembled horses,
oxen that resembled oxen,
and donkeys that resembled donkeys.
He was simply unable to move,
nor could he speak, nor could he eat.
The breath has no flesh, no skin, no organs, and no bones.
All its constituent elements are not explained in detail;
within all these elements, it is briefly described as being mostly invisible.
He taught the people how to discern what was good and what was bad;
thus, by tasting a small portion from among many dishes of food and drink,
he immediately knew which foods possessed flavor and which were flavorless.
However, for those who serve the Honored One,
one should expound the meaning of the sutras and compose this very scripture for them.
All matters have much to be praised and many significant details.
The origins are few;
it merely serves the celestial deities and explains the meaning of the heavens.
There are those who, fearing the Dharma of the World-Honored One,
personally cultivate a virtuous mind and personally perform good deeds.
Furthermore, it is good for people to offer counsel;
such a person is one who receives the teachings of the Honored Celestial One and receives the precepts of the Honored Celestial One.
If a person constantly commits evil and teaches others to do evil,
this person does not receive the teachings of the Celestial Honored One.
Suddenly falling into the evil realms,
their lives fall under the dominion of King Yama.
There are those who receive the teachings of the Celestial Honored One.
I have always said that I receive the precepts and teach others to receive them.
People ought to revere the Honored One;
every day, they should admonish themselves against error.
All sentient beings are individually terrified by the Celestial Honored One, who binds and gathers them;
he governs and manages all beings through birth and death, binding and gathering their entire spirits.
If sentient beings fear the Celestial Honored One,
they should likewise stand in awe of the Sovereign;
for the Sovereign’s former life was one of merit and virtue, and it is the Celestial Honored One who has filled his office.
Furthermore, there is no self;
the Celestial Honored One is that which is produced by oneself.
O Sage, all sentient beings take refuge in the movements and conduct of the Sage.
If there is someone who does not accept [the commands] and refuses to submit to the service of the Sovereign,
that person among sentient beings is one who commits rebellion and must pay retribution.
If there is someone who receives the instructions and movements of the Sovereign...
They immediately became capable of understanding human affairs,
were submissive and obedient to his commands,
and became those who were pleasing to him.
Furthermore, by exhorting others to do good and refraining from doing evil oneself,
this person becomes a locus for receiving the precepts.
For example, if there is a person who receives the precepts yet does not revere the Honored One,
this person and that place where the Dharma and Vinaya are not established do not constitute a valid reception of the precepts.
Such a person is one who acts in rebellion.
Third, one must revere one's parents and serve them with devotion.
One should compare this to serving the Celestial Honored One and the Sage Emperor;
if a person has previously served the Celestial Honored One and the Sage Sovereign,
and has served their parents without deficiency, [they shall attain such merit].
This person attains merit from the World-Honored One that is not small; these are three matters.
The first is having previously served the World-Honored One.
The second matter concerns the Sovereign;
the third matter concerns one's parents.
For this reason, all those under heaven and upon the earth act as if they were their own parents.
Accordingly, His Majesty is born of the divine.
Although his parents still live in this world,
sentient beings who possess wisdom and discernment ought to stand in awe of the Celestial Honored One and His Majesty.
Furthermore, out of reverence for my parents,
I am eager to receive the Dharma teachings of the Celestial Honored One and must not violate the precepts.
Regarding that which the Celestial Honored One has received and the honored teachings he has received:
first, he dispatches sentient beings to pay homage to the various celestial Buddhas,
so that they may undergo suffering for the sake of the Buddha.
The establishment of heaven and earth is solely due to the causes and conditions of pure majestic power. Your Majesty need only diligently practice the sublime;
Your Majesty’s palace has been sought from all Buddhas, and Your Majesty’s entire person is entirely liberated.
The Celestial Honored One said:
"All sentient beings who revert to various evils and act in rebellion against the Honored One..."
This, too, is not filial piety.
As for the second vow:
if one is filial toward one's parents and serves them with reverence and care.
All sentient beings who filially support their parents and reverently serve them without fail shall,
at the time of their death, attain the heavenly realm; there,
they shall have that realm as their dwelling for the purpose of serving their parents.
If sentient beings had no parents,
from what source would they be born?
This is the fourth vow.
For example, when a person who has received the precepts directs a wholesome mind toward all sentient beings,
they must not harbor malice or ill will.
The fifth vow is:
May sentient beings not kill themselves,
nor urge others to kill.
Therefore, the lives of all sentient beings are no different from the life of a human being.
As for the sixth vow:
do not commit adultery with the wives and children of others, nor do you yourself be enticed by them.
The seventh vow is:
Do not commit theft.
The eighth is: When seeing the wealth of other sentient beings—including their riches, fields, houses, slaves, and celestial pleasures—do not harbor jealousy.
The ninth vow: To have excellent wives and children, as well as a magnificent golden house,
and to compose literary works and perform rites for others.
The tenth vow is: To receive items entrusted by others and to use them for their expenses.
The Celestial Honored One has issued instructions on this matter:
one must not show excessive weakness;
do not deceive others.
When seeing a poor child,
do not truly turn your face away;
when the family is starving, give them plenty to drink.
Regarding the matter of relinquishment:
for example, seeing a man exerting himself, one should diligently provide him with drink;
seeing a person without clothing, one should immediately give them clothing.
Do not allow the wealth and possessions accumulated for your children to remain for even a single day;
thus, the rules for raising children are merely a matter of degree,
yet one must not shun cold or freezing weather [in their service].
If one exerts effort and sees such [a person], one must not revile them.
The various deities possess great power;
if one adds to this by reviling them, one will certainly encounter calamities and obstacles.
If a poor person requires money,
you must give it to them if you have it; if you have no money to give, [you must speak the truth].
One should dispel [the notion of] giving to those who do not exist through reasoning.
When seeing others suffering from chronic illnesses,
one must truly not mock them.
"This person is not free.
Such a one is afflicted by disease, a poor child, without clothing, and tattered.
Truly, do not call him."
Do not deceive others to take their property;
do not wrong others. If someone comes forward with a grievance, [investigate it].
One should not suppress or terminate matters according to the facts.
When there are appeals from widowers, widows, orphans, or solitary women,
one must not harbor resentment or cause them injustice.
Do not allow resentment to arise.
Truly, do not harbor a haughty mind nor engage in self-aggrandizement.
Do not spread gossip or engage in idle chatter.
If you cause two people to fight and strike one another,
seek redress within this lifetime;
do not involve the prefectures or counties.
The official, acknowledging his ignorance,
replied once to the person receiving the precepts:
"Do not harbor ill will toward others."
All sentient beings should always give rise to wholesome thoughts;
do not wish for evil because of your own evil.
Thus, from the many, one selects the few.
One should constantly cultivate goodness toward all sentient beings.
It is as if someone were to see this and wish to know how to receive the precepts;
who is able to rely upon this sutra?
This refers to the person receiving the precepts.
If there are sentient beings who cannot abide by the instructions for one receiving the precepts,
these are all addressed by the World-Honored One toward the elders and toward those of both senior and junior standing.
It is well to welcome and offer counsel;
this is the first ordinance of the World-Honored One.
Sentient beings rely upon the World-Honored One as their refuge.
Do not allow sentient beings to be killed for sacrifice,
nor send forth those whose lives are at risk;
yet sentient beings do not rely upon this teaching.
They take life for sacrifices;
they eat meat and relish its flavor;
they deceive the gods with their offerings.
They would then slaughter sheep and other animals;
sentient beings do not follow this teaching,
but instead act as intermediaries for making favorable arrangements.
Sentient beings turn their backs on [the Dharma] and commit evil,
thereby turning their backs on the Celestial Honored One.
Seeing sentient beings in such a state, the Celestial Honored One feels compassion for them.
Although he was admonished many times,
he did not comply with doing good. The World-Honored One then sent a cool breeze toward a young girl named Mayā.
A cool breeze immediately entered the belly of Māyā;
in accordance with the teaching of the World-Honored One,
Māyā conceived a child at that very moment.
May the Honored One cause a cool breeze to attend upon the young maiden;
may she conceive without a husband,
and may all sentient beings witness her conceiving without a husband.
When people of the world see this, they immediately take it as the Way.
The World-Honored One possesses awesome power;
he immediately causes sentient beings to purify their faith and dedicate their merit toward wholesome conditions.
Moyan conceived and later gave birth to a son named Yishu;
his father was Xiang Liangfeng.
There are ignorant sentient beings who are themselves the Way.
If one faces the wind and gives birth with natural ease,
there shall be a single imperial decree issued by the Sage Sovereign of the World to the place where they reside.
All sentient beings joyfully submit to and rely upon this Celestial Honored One,
who dwells in the heavens and universally governs heaven and earth.
When the mouse moves from its birthplace, the abode of the Master of Delusion (Mihiraka) appears in the world; one sees the fruit of illumination existing within heaven and earth.
One knows that the Star of Pungency (Kṣipra) resides upon the heavens.
The stars were as large as chariot wheels;
their brilliance and purity were such that the abode of the World-Honored One was uniquely sublime.
Before and after [his birth], he was born in the city of Uruvilvā within the Veṇuvana grove.
One shall be born in Miśraka;
after five periods of one year have passed,
one will engage in speech and preach the Dharma.
Acting kindly toward sentient beings,
one who is over twelve years of age seeks [ordination] at a pure place; this is called the "Difficult Request."
The character [for "river"] refers to the Valley of Heat (Tánggǔ) for those who are spiritually obscured.
At first, Mīshéhědì was subdued; the Sage resided within the gorges, and from birth until his passing, he never consumed alcohol or meat.
They ate only raw vegetables and honey upon the ground.
At that time, there were sentient beings who did not frequently bow toward the valleys or perform prostrations in a state of confusion.
Furthermore, upon receiving the precepts,
one should immediately enter the *mishika* bathhouse at dusk to wash amidst the many hardships.
After the *mishika* has finished entering the hot water, he emerges from it.
Immediately, a cool breeze arose from the heavens;
his countenance appeared like a slightly opened door as he sat facing Maitreya.
In the space above, he asked the question:
"Mishaha is my son; among all sentient beings in the world..."
All who take up the instructions of Mithyāka perform their assigned tasks well;
thus, Mithyāka is like a being in the heavenly realms, for he acts according to the commands of this World-Honored One.
He commanded the inferior beings of the world to cease their activities and devote themselves to the spirits;
immediately, there were those who heard these words.
Cease from harmful deeds and spirits;
cease from doing evil,
and instead believe in and practice wholesome actions.
When Miśraka was twelve years old and Ki was thirty-two, they sought out all sentient beings who possessed evil karma and sent them back toward wholesome karma and the good paths.
Miśraka had twelve disciples.
Thereupon, those suffering were turned back;
those who could fly were restored to life,
and the blind regained their sight.
Those with unusual physical features were treated for chronic ailments;
those who were ill received medical care;
and those possessed by spirits were cured by chasing away the demons, though some remained lame.
All those who were ill sought out Miśraka and grasped his kāṣāya robe;
they all recovered from their ailments.
Furthermore, there was not a single person among those who committed evil deeds who failed to pass on to the good realms.
Those who do not believe in the teachings of the Celestial Honored One,
as well as those who are impure and greedy for profit,
shall not be released from this world.
They indulge in wine and eat meat,
and they serve spirits and deities;
these literary men persist in their adherence [to such practices], eventually fabricating false accounts or claiming to have witnessed them.
He then intended to kill [the Buddha].
Because there were many sentient beings for this reason,
they immediately believed in this teaching.
For this reason, he was unable to kill him.
Later, Miśraka, through the ripening of his evil karma, was reborn as a *śakunta* bird.
A person of pure faith then discussed the matter among themselves.
He then wished to kill Mīṣaḥa,
but seeing no way to accomplish this,
he went straight to the Great King.
Those who speak evil and perform evil deeds bring about misfortune;
Maitreya performs good.
He applies himself with even greater diligence to instruct sentient beings.
When he was over thirty-two years old,
those who were habitually wicked people spoke thus to the Great King Viradhasu:
He addressed Vīradatta, saying as before:
"Mithilaka deserves the death penalty.
The Great King immediately summoned the witnesses to verify the evil causes and conditions.
Miśraka went before King Virāṭuṣa; Miśraka was deemed deserving of the death penalty,
and the Great King immediately intended to carry out the execution.
That person deserves the death penalty.
I truly have neither heard nor seen it;
that person does not deserve to die.
"This matter must be severed by the person of evil affinity themselves.
The Great King said,
"I cannot kill this person of evil affinity."
He then said, "That man shall not die; he is my son.
Great King Virāṭu then sought water to wash his hands.
In the presence of adverse conditions and the like,
I truly cannot kill that person—
those who possess such adverse conditions.
He requested further clarification:
"Is it not the case that one cannot attain [liberation] without abstaining from killing?
Does Māṃsika offer his own body as a gift to the wicked?"
For the sake of all sentient beings, he causes worldly people and others to know that human life is like a flickering candle;
for the sake of sentient beings of the present age, he gives his own life as an offering in exchange for their lives, accepting death on their behalf.
Miśraka led himself and Suiji (Sudṛṣṭi) to their deaths;
the person of evil karma then took Miśraka elsewhere,
to the place where the bathing ladles were kept.
It was called "Kṣu" (the end).
He then tied it to a tree and further took two more people who were practitioners of the Path.
That person stands to the right;
the day is approaching Mīṣaka,
and he is bound upon the wooden stake for five periods.
This is the six-day fast.
One binds oneself at dawn,
and continues until sunset.
The four quarters were shrouded in darkness, the earth shook, and mountains collapsed.
All the gates of the cemeteries in the world opened,
and all those who were dead were restored to life.
When such a person sees this, they likewise lack faith in the scriptural teachings.
Whether alive or dead, Maitreya rebukes that person; the person then immediately says: "I have great faith."
